summary: Iteration 3 backend-only re-test of UnlockVault focusing on new concurrent match-passwords and unlock behaviour. Re-ran existing pytest suite (22 regression tests) and added 2 new concurrency-correctness tests. All 24/24 pass in ~9s on the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL.
critical_code_review_comments: Concurrency hardening (asyncio.to_thread + Semaphore(8)) in /api/match-passwords and /api/unlock is correct: each file independently finds its own password; a non-matching file stays locked and does not get a wrong password assigned from another file's list (no cross-contamination).
Minor pytest deprecation warning: class-scoped fixture defined as instance method in TestConcurrency - cosmetic, suite still green. Can be refactored to @classmethod if desired.
test_credentials: No auth. Session IDs auto-generated per test. Locked PDF password: 'pw123' (single-file flow); concurrency test creates /tmp/locked_0..5.pdf with passwords secret0..secret5 and one non-matching file with pw 'zzz_unique_999'.
seed_data_creation: Dynamic: /tmp/locked_{0..5}.pdf and /tmp/locked_nomatch.pdf generated at test time via pikepdf.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite /app/backend/tests/test_unlockvault.py now covers: security (invalid session_id), full flow (upload/match/unlock/download/zip/merge/replace/delete), extras (too-many-files, generic unlock error), and concurrency correctness (6 distinct locked PDFs matched to their own passwords in parallel + unlocked concurrently + downloads open without password). Excel verify_password branch not exercised directly (no locked .xlsx fixture); PDF concurrent branch fully validated.
rca of the issue: N/A - no bugs found this iteration. Previously reported slowness is resolved: 6 locked PDFs x 9 candidate passwords completes in ~1-2s thanks to Semaphore(8) + asyncio.to_thread.
